embeds.title: 🔴 Microsoft Shares Mitigation for YellowKey Windows Zero-Day
embeds.description:
Microsoft has released mitigation guidance for YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585), a Windows BitLocker zero-day vulnerability disclosed by anonymous researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse'. The flaw allows access to BitLocker-protected drives through specially crafted FsTx files on USB drives or EFI partitions. Microsoft recommends removing autofstx.exe from BootExecute registry values and configuring BitLocker to TPM+PIN mode. The researcher has also disclosed multiple other zero-day vulnerabilities including BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825), RedSun, GreenPlasma, and UnDefend, reportedly in protest of Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure handling.

embeds.title: 🟢 Microsoft Releases Mitigation for BitLocker Bypass Vulnerability YellowKey
embeds.description:
Microsoft released a mitigation for CVE-2026-45585, a BitLocker security feature bypass vulnerability named YellowKey that was publicly disclosed by security researcher Chaotic Eclipse. The zero-day flaw (CVSS 6.8) allows an attacker with physical access to bypass BitLocker Device Encryption by placing specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive or EFI partition and exploiting the Windows Recovery Environment. The vulnerability affects Windows 11 versions 26H1, 24H2, and 25H2 for x64-based systems, as well as Windows Server 2025. Microsoft provided technical mitigations including removing autofstx.exe from WinRE and switching BitLocker protection from TPM-only to TPM+PIN mode.
**Sources:** thehackernews.com • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-45585 • **Access:** Physical access with USB drive containing specially crafted FsTx files
